title: The Coming Taiwan Crisis
gist: Czin argues the Taiwan Strait's current calm reflects Xi's optimism about a KMT return, but the real pivot is 2028 (US and Taiwan elections), when a likely-frustrated, aging Xi may escalate coercion short of invasion. He urges Washington to use the 2026-2028 window to approve the $14B arms package and back a decoupled, defense-reforming Taiwan.

insights.claim: The 2027 PLA readiness deadline is unlikely to trigger Chinese use of lethal force against Taiwan; the real pivot point is 2028, when both the US and Taiwan hold presidential elections.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Shifts the tail-risk window for Taiwan-exposed assets (semis, shipping, regional equities) from 2027 to post-2028.
insights.quote: The next pivotal date will not be 2027, when Xi is expected to begin a fourth term, but 2028

insights.claim: Xi's willingness to conduct systematic purges of the PLA high command signals he does not expect a cross-strait crisis in the near term.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Military purges are a readable indicator of near-term conflict intent; their completion could flag rising risk.
insights.quote: Xi has been willing to conduct systematic purges of his military high command, in part because he is not worried about a cross-strait crisis in the near future.

insights.claim: Beijing has avoided large-scale military exercises around Taiwan for nearly a year, a shift driven by renewed optimism after Trump's comments weakened Taipei's confidence in US commitment.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Current calm reflects Chinese optimism, not reduced intent, so it can reverse quickly if that optimism fades.
insights.quote: for nearly a year, Beijing has avoided the large-scale military exercises

insights.claim: Xi will likely be frustrated by Taiwan's 2028 election result, making the post-2028 period in the Taiwan Strait far more turbulent than today.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Implies elevated geopolitical risk premium for Taiwan/semiconductor supply chains from 2028 onward.
insights.quote: In all likelihood, Xi will find himself frustrated by the outcome of Taiwan’s next election

insights.claim: By the end of a fourth term Xi will be nearly 80, making him more impatient and likelier to conclude that further delay on Taiwan no longer serves him.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Leader age creates a time-decaying patience function that raises coercion risk later in the decade.
insights.quote: by the end of it, he will be nearly 80
insights.locator: Xi is likely to be more

themes.theme: KMT bet and Beijing's hollow strategy

insights.claim: Xi's optimism hinges on the KMT regaining power in 2028, with KMT chair Cheng Li-wun as the linchpin, but her prospects are precarious: she won the chair with just over 50% and only 27% of the population supports the KMT.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Beijing's peaceful-path thesis rests on a weak political base, raising odds of disappointment and escalation.
insights.quote: only 27 percent of the population supports her party

insights.claim: Xi's ultimate goal is political annexation of Taiwan rather than a costly and likely catastrophic military invasion.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Base case is grey-zone coercion and political pressure, not invasion; price risk accordingly.
insights.quote: Annexation, not a costly and likely catastrophic military invasion, is his ultimate goal.

insights.claim: A second Lai Ching-te term with a renewed legislative majority would devastate Xi's hope that the KMT is a viable alternative and leave him steward of a Taiwan policy with no progress in over a dozen years.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: A DPP sweep in 2028 is the key trigger scenario to watch for escalation risk.
insights.quote: Should Lai secure a second term along with a renewed majority in Taiwan’s Legislative Yuan, it would devastate Xi’s hope

insights.claim: Both Hu Jintao's soft approach (backfiring via the 2014 Sunflower Movement) and Xi's post-2016 coercion-without-diplomacy have failed to move Taiwan toward the mainland, exposing the CCP strategy as hollow.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Neither carrot nor stick has worked, narrowing Beijing's options toward riskier tools over time.
insights.quote: Xi’s looming dilemma underscores the hollowness of the Chinese Communist Party’s Taiwan strategy.

insights.claim: A frustrated Xi could move beyond his 2022 response to a sustained punitive pressure campaign short of blockade: stopping foreign ships, declaring multiple no-go maritime zones, and disrupting US arms deliveries on commercial carriers.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Partial maritime disruption is a plausible scenario hitting shipping, insurance and chip logistics without a formal blockade.
insights.quote: stopping foreign ships at sea, declaring multiple zones near Taiwan off-limits to international maritime traffic
insights.locator: But Xi would have to go

insights.claim: The 2022 Pelosi episode taught Xi he can go quite far, including missile overflights and maritime exclusion zones, without provoking a full US crisis or tangible costs for China.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Lack of past costs lowers Beijing's perceived price of future coercion.
insights.quote: Yet it did not provoke a full-blown crisis with the United States or cause tangible repercussions for China.
insights.locator: Xi is likely to be more

insights.claim: Chinese escalation could backfire by triggering a rally-around-the-flag effect in Taiwan, as when 1990s threats helped the DPP win its first presidential race in 2000.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Coercion may entrench the outcome Beijing opposes, prolonging rather than resolving the standoff.
insights.quote: it might just as easily backfire, creating a rally-around-the-flag effect on the island

insights.claim: Over 14 years Xi has shown he is neither impulsive nor especially violent, preferring incremental pressure; a blockade or quarantine would play to US strengths by giving time to build a coalition to impose costs.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Lowers probability of sudden blockade; favors slow-burn pressure scenarios.
insights.quote: preferring steady, incremental pressure over a single decisive blow

insights.claim: A 'restrainer' US president skeptical of alliances after 2028 would make more violent Chinese options more tempting.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: US 2028 election outcome is a direct input to Taiwan risk pricing.

insights.claim: The current war in Iran has depleted key US munitions stocks for years and exposed the vulnerability of US overseas bases and naval logistics, constraining US crisis response to China into the next administration.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Supports long-duration defense-industrial demand (munitions) and weaker US deterrence in Asia.
insights.quote: Key U.S. munitions stocks will take years to rebuild

themes.theme: Taiwan as model partner: defense and economy

insights.claim: Taiwan passed a $25 billion supplemental military appropriation in May, with the most contested issue being funding to expand its domestic drone industry.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Signals sustained Taiwanese defense spending, including domestic drone production.
insights.quote: In May, it passed a supplemental bill appropriating $25 billion for the military.

insights.claim: Taiwan's outbound investment going to China fell from more than 80% in 2010 to less than 10% today.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Dramatic economic decoupling reduces Beijing's economic leverage over Taiwan.
insights.quote: Whereas in 2010 more than 80 percent of Taiwan’s outbound investment went to China, today less than ten percent does.

insights.claim: Driven by its AI-boosted semiconductor industry, Taiwan (population 23 million) has become the fourth-largest US trading partner and its leading firms pledged hundreds of billions in US investment.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Confirms Taiwan's centrality to the AI hardware supply chain and onshoring capex in the US.
insights.quote: Taiwan has catapulted to become the fourth-largest trading partner of the United States

insights.claim: Taiwan's February trade deal with the Trump administration pleased Taipei because it narrowed the tariff gap versus Japan and South Korea.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Tariff parity improves Taiwanese exporters' competitiveness against regional rivals.
insights.quote: it narrows the gap between the tariff rate on Taiwan’s goods and the rates on goods from its regional competitors Japan and South Korea

insights.claim: Taiwan's government is pursuing whole-of-society resilience and keeping 'red' Chinese components out of government procurement supply chains.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Procurement exclusion of Chinese components benefits non-Chinese suppliers in Taiwan's public spending.
insights.quote: the government is intent on keeping “red” components out of supply chains for government procurement

themes.theme: US policy: arms sales as weakest link

insights.claim: Trump should approve the pending $14 billion Taiwan arms package, even in smaller tranches, because Beijing cares more about high-profile political gestures than bureaucratic arms transfers.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Approval would be a material defense-contractor catalyst and a signal on US Taiwan commitment.
insights.quote: At the very least, Trump should approve the $14 billion arms package that is on his desk

insights.claim: Leaving arms sales in abeyance risks letting Beijing establish a de facto veto over US arms sales and the cross-strait dynamic.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Precedent shift would weaken US deterrence credibility and Taiwan's defense trajectory.
insights.quote: the administration will be complicit in Beijing’s bid to establish a veto over U.S. arms sales

insights.claim: Trump described arms sales to Taiwan as a bargaining chip with Beijing, breaking decades of precedent that US presidents do not consult Chinese leaders on the subject.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Arms sales becoming transactional adds policy uncertainty for Taiwan-linked defense flows.

insights.claim: US defense-industrial deficiencies mean the $14 billion package would not arrive before the end of Trump's term, explaining his lack of enthusiasm, yet long lead times argue for acting now.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: Highlights US defense-industrial capacity bottlenecks as a structural constraint.
insights.quote: the capabilities in that package would not arrive in Taiwan before the end of Trump’s term
insights.locator: More seasoned observers of U.S. policy

insights.claim: Structural forces favor closer US-Taiwan ties, but diplomacy has become the weakest pillar; a KMT win in 2028 could also reduce Taiwan's enthusiasm for defense cooperation.
insights.speaker: Jonathan A. Czin
insights.so_what: The 2026-2028 window is when US-Taiwan defense deals are most feasible.
insights.quote: The structural forces all favor a closer relationship, but the diplomacy—which should be the easiest part of getting this right—has become the weakest pillar.
